newsitem.title: USA: Millon hopes to fly again soon says top official.
newsitem.headline: Millon hopes to fly again soon says top official.

text.p: Millon Air, which has been grounded since an accident in October, hopes to be revalidated to fly again soon, a top executive said Wednesday.
"It is going very smoothly. We have an extremely good team from the Federal Aviation Adminsitration(FAA) working with us," John Bonner, Millon's general manager, told Reuters.
The all-cargo, Miami-based airline hopes it could be back in the air in as soon as a few weeks, Bonner said.
A Millon Boeing 707 crashed into a residential area of Manta, Ecuador on October 22, killing the flight crew and at least 20 people on the ground.
After the accident, Millon was allowed to wet-lease aircraft for 30 days. Following that 30-day period, Millon applied to wet-lease aircraft so it could continue to serve its customers.
It applied to the U.S. Department of Transportation(DOT) for wet-lease authority to Jamaica, Venezuela, Bolivia and Brazil.
The DOT denied its application in January, Department spokesman Bill Mosley said.
Family-owned Millon, which normally has about 125 employees, has had to lay-off about two-thirds of them, Bonner said.
